title: Calibrated spin models better matched a measured diamond ensemble spectrum
summary: For a measured zero-field nitrogen-vacancy ensemble spectrum, calibrating effective spin-model terms reduced held-frequency error from 0.008835 to 0.003872 across four folds. The source models were learned from single-center spectra, and both comparisons fitted the same linewidth and optical-readout terms.
ai_technology: Symbolic regression; learned effective spin Hamiltonians
organization: University of New South Wales; Cryo-X Tech; Xidian University

source_review.scope: primary v1-only PDF learned source models and Section IV experimental ensemble fits

evidence.tested: The authors used a matched comparison across held frequencies in a 38-point experimental scan and froze each learned source expression before fitting the target ensemble.
evidence.unknown: Other effective compositions can produce comparable spectra, so this does not uniquely determine microscopic parameters. The independent field-condition test reported elsewhere in the paper uses simulation.
evidence.ai_role: Constrained symbolic regression selected and fitted spin Hamiltonian models from measured single-center spectra. The models formed the starting point for ensemble calibration.
